posts.title: Bags down. Vacation on.
posts.headline:
Bags down.
Vacation on.
posts.sub:
A warm welcome. The useful details.
One place to find them.
posts.alt: Two travelers with backpacks look at a phone inside a timber building. A short DigiStayBook headline introduces a welcoming guest guide.
posts.caption:
Bags down. Shoes off. Now, where’s the Wi-Fi?

The first few minutes in a vacation rental come with little questions. Put your welcome, house essentials and local tips together in DigiStayBook, so guests have somewhere to look when they arrive.

One property QR display opens the guest page in their browser. No guest app or account needed.

Take a look around the demo:
https://digistaybook.com/stay/demo-cottage?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=people_moments_20261029&utm_content=01-arrival

posts.note: Stock travelers illustrate arrival. The original phone screen is unchanged; this is not a recorded customer session.

posts.title: The first coffee can wait. The Wi-Fi question won’t.
posts.headline:
First coffee.
Then the day.
posts.sub:
House essentials, right there
when guests need them.
posts.alt: A couple smiles at a smartphone in a kitchen. Beside the headline is a separate, labeled capture of the fictional DigiStayBook guest demo.
posts.caption:
The kettle’s on. Someone’s looking up breakfast. Someone else needs the Wi-Fi.

These are the little moments a guest guide is for. Keep practical details and your own welcome together on the DigiStayBook guest page.

Guests open it in their browser from your property QR display.

posts.title: Send them to your favorite little spot.
posts.headline:
Your local knowledge.
Their kind of morning.
posts.sub: Share the places you’d send a friend.
posts.alt: A couple enjoys takeout coffee outdoors. A dark panel beneath the photo invites hosts to share their own local favorites.
posts.caption:
You know the coffee worth walking for. The bakery that sells out early. The quieter way down to the beach.

That’s the kind of local knowledge guests can’t get from a list of house rules.

Add your own favorites to your DigiStayBook welcome, so guests can find a little of what you love about the area.

Explore the guest demo:
https://digistaybook.com/stay/demo-cottage?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=people_moments_20261029&utm_content=03-local

Stock photography used for illustration.
posts.note: Stock café scene; no specific café, business partnership or customer recommendation is claimed.

posts.title: Rain outside. A good stay inside.
posts.headline:
Rain outside.
A good stay inside.
posts.sub: Tell them where the good stuff is.
posts.alt: A family gathers around a table to play a game. The DigiStayBook post suggests making indoor activity details easy for guests to find.
posts.caption:
A rainy afternoon can still turn into a good vacation memory.

If your place has board games, books or a favorite rainy-day outing nearby, tell guests where to find them. A small note can make the things you’ve thoughtfully provided easier to enjoy.

DigiStayBook brings your house guidance and personal tips into one guest page.

See an example welcome:
https://digistaybook.com/stay/demo-cottage?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=people_moments_20261029&utm_content=04-rainy

Stock photography used for illustration.
posts.note: Stock family scene illustrates indoor time together. No weather event or actual DigiStayBook family is documented.

posts.title: They’ll take photos. Give one a home.
posts.headline:
They’ll take photos.
Give one a home.
posts.sub:
A photo. A little note.
A memory of their stay.
posts.alt: A woman holds a smartphone at the beach. The caption panel invites hosts to give guests a place to leave a photo and note about their stay.
posts.caption:
The beach walk. A slow morning. The moment everyone finally sat down together.

Your guests will take photos of their break. With DigiStayBook, you can invite them to leave a photo and a little note on your property’s guest wall too.

Keep the invitation simple, and let guests choose what they’d like to share.
